Height calculation adjusts to calc(100vh-12rem) with z-40 to maintain proper alignment and symmetric spacing during scroll. Change affects only the Web docs surface.

eli5.text: When you scroll down a documentation page, the table of contents on the left side now stays pinned to your screen instead of scrolling away with the rest of the content. Only people reading the web-based documentation will notice this; it doesn't affect the app or any other part of the product. If you open a docs page today and start scrolling, you'll see the sidebar holding its position as you move through the page.

ai.title: Docs sidebar gradient fades and custom scrollbar
ai.summary: Added dynamic top/bottom gradient fades and custom scrollbar styles to the docs sidebar. Implemented scroll detection via `useRef` and `useEffect` in `web/src/app/docs/layout.tsx`. Updated `web/src/styles/globals.css` with `.custom-scrollbar` rules for Webkit and Firefox.

eli5.text: When you scroll through the documentation sidebar on the docs page, you'll now see soft gradient fades at the top and bottom of the list that appear and disappear as you move up and down. The scrollbar on that same sidebar also got a visual refresh with a thinner, rounded appearance that's consistent across browsers. These effects are live today and only affect the documentation sidebar in the web app; other pages and sidebars are unchanged.

ai.title: CodebuffClient drops binary check
ai.summary: CodebuffClient constructor removes execFileSync check for CODEBUFF_BINARY in PATH. Eliminates hard dependency on global codebuff installation for SDK initialization. Affects sdk/src/client.ts; binary resolution deferred.

eli5.text: When you use the assistant toolkit in your own app, it no longer stops you with an error if the main assistant program isn't installed in the usual spot. Instead, the toolkit waits to look for that program only when you actually start a coding task, so setting up the toolkit itself doesn't require the program to be present first. This affects anyone building with the software development kit, who will now see setup succeed even without the global installation already in place.

ai.title: Add reasoningOptions to agent templates
ai.summary: Introduced `reasoningOptions` in `AgentDefinition` and `DynamicAgentDefinitionSchema` to control OpenRouter reasoning tokens via `max_tokens` or `effort`. Backend `prompt-agent-stream.ts` maps these options to `providerOptions.openrouter.reasoning`, replacing hardcoded Gemini thinking configs. Scope covers core types, backend stream logic, and template definitions.

eli5.text: If you design a custom assistant and point it at a reasoning-capable model, you can now decide how much of that model's step-by-step thinking shows up in its reply. You do it by telling the assistant template to include a reasoning level (high, medium, or low), reserve a fixed number of thinking tokens, or turn reasoning off for that assistant. That choice sticks to the template instead of being baked into one specific provider, so the same setting can travel with the assistant as you swap models or move it between providers. The feature is in place and wired through the core assistant definitions and the streaming path that answers prompts, so it is live today for any assistant template built on these base definitions.

ai.title: SDK v0.1.9
ai.summary: Bumped @codebuff/sdk version to 0.1.9. Internal release increment. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The official software kit for connecting to Codebuff was repackaged internally with a fresh label. People building tools that talk to Codebuff will pull down this new version automatically when they update, but they won't see any new capabilities or changes in how it works. It's the same functionality as before, just re-tagged behind the scenes.

ai.title: Make reasoningOptions optional in AgentTemplate
ai.summary: Changed `reasoningOptions` to optional in `common/src/types/agent-template.ts`. Fixes typechecker errors where reasoning configuration was not strictly required.

eli5.text: You, the developer using the agent template feature, no longer have to provide a reasoning configuration when setting up an agent, if you don't need custom reasoning settings, you can simply leave that part out. The system already lets you add reasoning options to agent templates (as recorded in this snapshot), so making it optional just removes a strict requirement that was causing build errors when the field was missing. Nothing about how reasoning works changes; the feature is in place and live, and this change only stops the system from hard-failing when you omit an optional detail.

ai.title: Agent spawn matching uses parsed IDs
ai.summary: Exported parseAgentId from backend/src/templates/agent-registry.ts. Updated handleSpawnAgents in backend/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agents.ts to validate spawn permissions via getMatchingSpawn using parsed publisher, agent, and version IDs. Replaced strict string equality checks for spawnableAgents. Handles partial ID matching when version or publisher is omitted.

eli5.text: When you ask the system to spawn a new agent, it can now match agent IDs more flexibly. Instead of requiring an exact, full ID match, the system parses the publisher, agent name, and version separately and allows partial matches when version or publisher is omitted. This means spawn permissions are validated using these parsed components via a new matching function. You would notice that previously strict string equality checks have been replaced with logic that handles partial ID matching, making spawning work even with less specific IDs.

ai.title: Extract agent ID parsing utils to shared common module
ai.summary: Moved `parseAgentId` from `backend/src/templates/agent-registry.ts` to new `common/src/util/agent-id-parsing.ts`. Added `parsePublishedAgentId` for strict publisher/agent validation and updated `spawn-agents.ts` to handle optional fields. Refactors backend to rely on shared utilities for consistent agent ID parsing.

eli5.text: The system now has a single, shared set of rules for understanding agent IDs, identifiers that tell it which publisher and agent (and optional version) to use, instead of each component making up its own rules. This affects how the platform recognizes and matches agents when one agent tries to use another, and if you watched the process, you'd see the matching logic now consistently handles cases where a publisher prefix or version is missing rather than silently failing. The new parsing approach is live today as part of the updated agent spawning flow.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, engineers adjusted one of the system's internal parts so that a specific set of rules about which helper agents are allowed to team up can now be checked separately and more thoroughly. They also added a fresh collection of automated checks that put those teamwork rules through their paces. You wouldn't see anything new on your screen; this is housekeeping that helps the team catch mistakes faster and keep the helper-agent matching reliable.

ai.title: Docs: reasoningOptions agent field
ai.summary: Documents `reasoningOptions` for agent definitions in `agent-reference.mdx` and `customizing-agents.mdx`. Covers `enabled`, `exclude`, and `effort` fields using OpenRouter-style reasoning token budgets. Notes that unsupported models ignore these options. Adds usage examples for tuning reasoning effort.

eli5.text: The internal documentation for agent tools now includes a section on reasoning options, a feature that lets developers set a built-in assistant to think harder or faster before replying, but only if the model they pick actually supports it; these new fields are ignored quietly by models that don't. This is a small documentation update that adds examples for turning reasoning on and choosing an effort level, live today in the official agent guides.

ai.title: SDK adds custom tool support to agent prompt and stream parser
ai.summary: Custom tools defined in `fileContext.customToolDefinitions` are injected into agent prompts via `getToolsInstructions` and `getShortToolInstructions`, replacing strict `ToolName[]` types with `readonly string[]`. The stream parser registers `customToolCallback` for each custom tool, delegating execution to `executeCustomToolCall` in `tool-executor.ts`. `paramsSection` now accepts both Zod and raw JSON schemas, converting JSON to Zod via `convertJsonSchemaToZod` for validation. `add-message.ts` and `set-messages.ts` tool descriptions were re-indented.

eli5.text: The AI assistant you talk to can now use your own custom tools that you define, not just the built-in ones. When you give it a project, any custom tools you've set up are now included in the instructions the assistant reads, so it knows what extra commands are available and can run them during the conversation. The assistant also understands your tools even if they're described using standard JSON schema format, not just its native format. If you looked at how the assistant talks about its available commands, you'd see your custom tools listed alongside the built-in ones, properly formatted in the examples it shows.
